citation.title: Positive End-Expiratory Pressure Setting in COVID-19-Related Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Comparison Between Electrical Impedance Tomography, PEEP/FiO2 Tables, and Transpulmonary Pressure

provenance.quote: we enrolled the patients with 2019 coronavirus disease (COVID-19)-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), who required mechanical ventilation and were admitted to the ICU
All patients were ventilated in volume control mode
admitted to our Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
PEEP as based upon end-expiratory PL/FiO2 table, was applied (3).
Respiratory mechanics variables were recorded.
Seventeen patients (15 men, 2 women) were enrolled.
We describe a case series of patients suffering from 2019 coronavirus disease (COVID-19)-related ARDS in whom we compared PEEP settings based on PEEP/FiO2 tables, PL/FiO2 table, and EIT.
Frontiers in Medicine

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ARDS: all patients had COVID-19-related moderate-to-severe ARDS. Obesity: median BMI 31.1 kg/m2. Timing: measurements after 24-48 h of mechanical ventilation, so early. PTP target: strategy was PL/FiO2 table aiming for positive end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure, based on general description 'PEEP has to be set to maintain the end-expiratory PL above zero'.

unclear_items: adults_18_plus: no explicit age criterion; adult ICU inferred.

country: France inferred from affiliation; not explicitly stated.
n_neuromuscular_blockade: all patients paralyzed during measurement, but no count reported.
enrolment_end: not reported; assumed to be March 2021.
extraction_flags.general_notes: The study's primary focus is comparing EIT-guided PEEP with PEEP/FiO2 tables and PL/FiO2 table. The PL/FiO2 arm is the esophageal balloon-guided intervention.
